correctness.rationale: The lower bound is the published Griesmer bound for n_q(k,d,r). For every residue class modulo 9 from d=4 onward, an explicit multiset in PG(2,3) meets that bound; adding one full projective plane increases length by 13 and distance by 9 while preserving locality 2. The nine bases are checked line-by-line and by direct enumeration of all 26 nonzero messages. Separate dual/parity-check arguments prove the small lower bounds at lengths 4 and 5. The verifier independently reconstructs PG(2,3), the bases, the small witnesses, and all lifted instances through d=1000. No finite enumeration is used to infer the infinite claim.

The 2017 ternary Singleton-optimal classification covers initial dimension-three locality-2 cases only through distance 6, not the all-distance minimum-length function. published-finding corpus and web searches in native, equivalent, projective, and Griesmer formulations found no complete ternary dimension-three locality-2 profile. value.rationale: The anchor paper treats exact minimum length n_q(k,d,r) as its central invariant, completely solves the nearby binary locality-2 problem in low dimensions, and leaves the ternary side with only selected numerical results. The finding gives a complete all-distance ternary dimension-three locality-2 profile and the sharp threshold at which locality becomes free relative to the Griesmer bound. The nine-residue projective construction is structural and reusable, rather than an isolated finite parameter computation.
